title: SIU investigates death of robbery suspect, 17
article: It was a New Year's Eve robbery gone terribly wrong and now provincial investigators are trying to piece together how a 17-year-old boy with a shotgun in his hands ended up dead by a police bullet. The Special Investigations Unit, which probes all police actions that result in serious injury or death, said in a statement on the weekend that it has assigned nine investigators to the case and is looking for witnesses to the dramatic confrontation in Toronto's east end.
The unit says it has designated one police officer as a "subject officer," whose conduct is being investigated and who is not obligated to submit to an interview by investigators.

While the 17-year-old -- whose name was not released by the SIU -- was killed, police were still looking yesterday for his three accomplices. All three sped off in a stolen van after the botched robbery. They were dressed in dark clothing and are believed to be between 18 and 23 years of age.

According to a police statement, the four were armed with three shotguns, two of which were sawed-off, when they entered the Windjammer Sports store on Danforth Avenue, near Woodbine Avenue, shortly before 6 p.m. on Friday.
Confronting two men inside, the youths loaded up with clothing from the store. But somehow the police were called to the address.
Police Chief Julian Fantino said that an officer from 55 Division ended up outside the store, face-to-face with the 17-year-old who pointed his shotgun at the officer.
"Fearing for his life, the police officer discharged his service firearm," Chief Fantino said in a statement.
The boy, reportedly shot in the chest, managed to run off and was found collapsed near Main Street and Danforth Avenue. He was pronounced dead at St. Michael's Hospital a short time later.
"I thought it was a few cars backfiring," said a neighbour who did not want to be identified, but who heard the gunshots that night. The area was quickly crawling with police cruisers.

The Toronto Police holdup squad was still looking for three other thieves, whom they describe as armed and dangerous. Any one with information was asked to phone the holdup squad at 416-808-7350 or Crime Stoppers at 416-222-TIPS (8477).
The incident was the sixth and final fatal police shooting of 2004. In four of the previous five killings, the SIU has cleared the officers involved of any wrongdoing.

On Aug. 25, a tactical-squad sharpshooter killed 45-year-old Sugston Anthony (Tony) Brookes, who had taken a woman hostage in front of Union Station during morning rush hour, holding what turned out to be a jammed gun to her head. Mr. Brookes, who had a history of domestic violence, had just tried to kill his estranged wife.
On June 13, police shot and killed O'brien Christopher-Reid, 26, after he charged at police. He had been wandering shirtless around Edwards Gardens and brandishing a knife.

On May 21, a plainclothes officer fatally shot 17-year-old Jeffrey Reodica three times in the back after the Scarborough teenager attacked an officer with a knife, an SIU report concluded. Jeffrey's family has condemned the report as a "whitewash."

On Jan. 10, an officer shot and killed 63-year-old Antonio Bellon, who had just fired a shotgun and wounded an officer in a confrontation with police in an alleyway near Dufferin Street and Rogers Road.

The SIU is continuing its investigation of a fatal shooting on Oct. 14. A plainclothes officer shot and killed Courtney Peters, 32, during a takedown of a suspected cocaine dealer at a Petro-Canada gas station at Ellesmere Road and Victoria Park Avenue.
